answer_html:

steps: Both of you go together to a Cook County Clerk Vital Records office (downtown: 118 N. Clark St., Room 120), with valid ID showing proof of age; you can start the application online first.
Sign the application and pay the $60 marriage license fee; the license is issued while you wait.
Wait 1 day: the license takes effect 1 day after it is issued and is valid for 60 days, for ceremonies in Chicago and suburban Cook County only.

Get married with your own officiant, or in person before a Cook County judge at the Marriage and Civil Union Court, 119 W. Randolph St. (lower level), Tuesday to Friday, no appointment; bring the license, ID and the $10 administrative fee.
Make sure the signed license is returned to the Clerk within 10 days after the ceremony; a certified copy of the certificate is $15.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get married in a Chicago courthouse?
faq.a: As of Oct 28, 2026, the Cook County Clerk charges $60 for the marriage license and the Circuit Court of Cook County asks a $10 administrative fee for an in-person civil ceremony: $70 in all. Certified copies of the marriage certificate are extra ($15, and $4 for each additional copy).

faq.q: Where do you get married at the courthouse in Chicago?
faq.a: In-person civil ceremonies are held at the Marriage and Civil Union Court, 119 W. Randolph St. (lower level), where a Cook County judge marries you. You first get the license at a Clerk's Vital Records office; downtown it is 118 N. Clark St., Room 120.

faq.q: What days can you get married at the courthouse in Chicago?
faq.a: In person, Tuesday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. and 2 p.m. to 4 p.m., plus Saturdays 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. by appointment only. Virtual (Zoom) ceremonies are on Mondays, by appointment.

faq.q: How long does it take to get married at the courthouse in Chicago?
faq.a: The Clerk issues the license while you wait, but it takes effect 1 day after it is issued, so the earliest ceremony is the next day (the license is valid for 60 days). The court takes no appointment for an in-person ceremony Tuesday to Friday; arrive no later than 30 minutes before closing.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to get married at a courthouse?
faq.a: The official fees here total $70. The lowest small-venue price we verified in Chicago is $400 (Garfield Park Conservatory: Jensen Room), so the courthouse is the cheaper start; see both pages before you decide.

tips.t: A short or midi white dress, a slip dress or a jumpsuit is easy in a courthouse hallway and looks great in photos. Bring a light jacket or wrap.
The court takes no appointment Tuesday to Friday. Go at the start of a session (9 a.m. or 2 p.m.) and arrive 30 minutes before closing at the latest.
Use the building: the front steps, a staircase, a big window. Ask the court if photos are allowed inside before you plan them, then walk a few minutes for a second backdrop.
Two to six people is easy to seat at lunch afterwards. Ask one friend to take photos so your photographer budget can go to the dress.
Call a restaurant a week ahead and ask for a table for your group. Order a set menu so the bill is no surprise.
